goalContext.title: Oxidationsprodukte von Alkanolen erklären
goalContext.description: Die lernende Person kann die Bildung von Aldehyden, Ketonen und Carbonsäuren bei der Oxidation geeigneter Alkanole erklären.

findings.evidence: Candidate ethanol explicitly shows CH3–CH2–OH: first C bonds to three H and second C; second C bonds to first C, upper H, right H and lower OH. Original source lacks the right H/bond at the OH-bearing carbon.

Ethanal/acetaldehyde CH3–CHO, ethanoic acid CH3–COOH, propan-2-ol (CH3)2CH–OH, propanone (CH3)2C=O and tert-butanol (CH3)3C–OH preserve C valence four, O valence two and H valence one. Product class labels fit the explicitly depicted examples.
Keine Carbonylbildung (ohne C–C-Spaltung) correctly limits the illustrated alcohol-to-carbonyl conversion. It does not make an absolute claim that tertiary alcohols cannot react under any conditions.

+[O] and arrows communicate oxidation classes. They are not balanced complete chemical reaction equations; no quantitative stoichiometry is claimed. The primary column depicts successive oxidation to aldehyde then acid.

Actually viewed 360×201 capture: explicit additional ethanol H and bond, double C=O bonds, CH3 groups, three alcohol classes, product labels and the C–C-cleavage condition remain distinguishable. This is compact illustration text; full native image remains preferable for detailed inspection.

Actually viewed 680×380 and 1678×937 images: no clipping or collided bonds; the tertiary condition and complete ethanol structure are clear. Three-column friendly style and white background remain consistent with the original.
